missing_project_scope.summary: Project-scoped read request did not include a project.
missing_project_scope.why: Project data is intentionally scoped. The system should not answer by scanning every project or silently falling back to a default project.
missing_project_scope.likely_source: The user or host omitted the project field for a project-scoped query.

project_memory_not_initialized.summary: Project memory appears uninitialized or too sparse for reliable task work.
project_memory_not_initialized.why: Cold-start and onboarding should be explicit. The agent needs a readiness packet, blocking gaps, and a safe initialization path instead of treating an empty read as success.
project_memory_not_initialized.likely_source: The selected project has no indexed components, overview, laws, or task context yet, or the agent omitted the explicit cold-start readiness step.

work_started_without_claim_or_missing_to.summary: Task-bound progress was submitted without active ownership proof.
work_started_without_claim_or_missing_to.why: Implementation work should begin only after start_task returns work_token, so the system can provide stage guidance, enforce ownership, and keep an auditable work trail.
work_started_without_claim_or_missing_to.likely_source: No active owned claim was found, or the work_token/session identity did not match the active claim.

ambiguous_public_ref.summary: A short public reference matched more than one artifact.
ambiguous_public_ref.why: Short ids are convenient, but the system must not guess when multiple durable refs match the same prefix.
ambiguous_public_ref.likely_source: The supplied ref/id prefix is too short for the current project data.

public_ref_not_found.summary: The requested public reference did not resolve through the read surface.
public_ref_not_found.why: The ref may be mistyped, stale, from another project alias, or not yet indexed in the public ref table.
public_ref_not_found.likely_source: The user or agent supplied a ref that is not currently resolvable in the selected project scope.

unknown_mailbox_form.summary: The submitted mailbox form is not known to the current public workflow.
unknown_mailbox_form.why: Mailbox forms are state-machine actions. The server should reject unknown forms instead of guessing a mutating operation.
unknown_mailbox_form.likely_source: The agent used an old tool name, a typo, or an internal form that is not exposed by the current mailbox state.

form_unavailable_in_state.summary: The submitted mailbox form is not available in the current workflow state.
form_unavailable_in_state.why: Workflow state controls which actions are safe. The server should explain the state mismatch and ask the agent to request the current state packet.
form_unavailable_in_state.likely_source: The agent reused a form from an earlier state, the host restarted, or the workflow advanced while the agent kept an old packet.

missing_required_fields.summary: The submitted public form is missing required fields.
missing_required_fields.why: Public forms are intentionally explicit so weak clients can repair one field list instead of guessing hidden defaults.
missing_required_fields.likely_source: The agent submitted a partial form payload or copied a recommended call without filling all required fields.

mailbox_action_conflict.summary: The mailbox form was valid, but the server-side action could not complete safely.
mailbox_action_conflict.why: Some failures happen after form validation: ownership checks, closeout evidence checks, stale task identity, or action-specific guardrails may still reject the operation.
mailbox_action_conflict.likely_source: The agent has a valid public form but missing or stale runtime evidence for the requested transition.

completion_requires_owned_claim.summary: Completed task closure requires an owned task claim and completion evidence.
completion_requires_owned_claim.why: Marking work completed is stronger than archiving obsolete work. The system requires ownership proof before accepting completed status.
completion_requires_owned_claim.likely_source: The agent tried to close a task as completed through a cleanup form instead of claiming the task and submitting finish_task with work_token.

edit_authority_scope_drift.summary: The approved project-editing framing no longer matches the work being considered.
edit_authority_scope_drift.why: Explicit approval applies only to the latest user-visible framing. New causes, solution directions, subsystems, behaviors, risks, completion criteria, change sets, or ambiguity require renewed approval; separate work should be captured as an improvement instead of expanding the current task.
edit_authority_scope_drift.likely_source: The agent discovered a new hypothesis or expanded the task after implementation authority was granted.

autonomous_mode_denied.summary: The requested task or action is outside the explicit autonomous-mode grant.
autonomous_mode_denied.why: Autonomous mode is deny-by-default. Only the exhaustive approved task list, matching framing versions, allowed actions, validity window, and separate commit/live permissions grant authority.
autonomous_mode_denied.likely_source: The grant expired, was revoked, omitted the task or action, or no longer matches the approved framing version.

route_misclassification.summary: A request appears to have routed to the wrong public facade or tool.
route_misclassification.why: Wrong route selection can make an agent act on a misleading answer even when the underlying data is healthy. The system should expose a compact public incident and a safe retry path instead of requiring internal telemetry.
route_misclassification.likely_source: The request wording was ambiguous, a learned route overmatched, or the expected facade/tool was not explicit enough.

stale_learned_route.summary: A learned route pattern appears stale or misleading and was invalidated.
stale_learned_route.why: Learned route aliases improve weak-client ergonomics, but stale aliases can keep sending similar requests to the wrong route until feedback disables or repairs them.
stale_learned_route.likely_source: A previously useful learned phrase no longer matches the current route contract or was trained from an over-broad example.

ambiguous_route_selection.summary: The request had multiple plausible route interpretations.
ambiguous_route_selection.why: When route candidates are close, the safest public response is to ask for a more explicit route or provide a diagnostic retry rather than silently trusting a weak match.
ambiguous_route_selection.likely_source: The request mixes lifecycle, read, feedback, or creation terms without a clear primary intent.
